replacements.before: A secure job can become more than employment. It can stand for a family’s hopes, the ability to repay a loan and relief from being dependent on someone else. **ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)** places that desire beside a father’s illness, until the son’s hope for security becomes entangled with the possibility of loss.
replacements.after: Four applicants sit shoulder to shoulder at 00:19 in the official trailer for **ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)**. Books and papers rest on their laps. Sanjay, in a pale shirt, turns towards the woman beside him and gestures towards her book; the two men to his other side look down at their reading material. The row fills the frame. Waiting takes a visible form here: bodies close together, pages held within reach, one person turning towards another while the others keep their attention on what they are reading.[^trailer-frame]

replacements.after: At 01:05 in Film Heritage Foundation’s restoration-comparison excerpt, an older man in white leans forward, his hands near his chin. The long back of his chair rises behind him, unoccupied by his body. Dark openings interrupt the pale wall around the seated figure.[^comparison-frame] The contrast is worth staying with: the chair offers room to lean back, while his posture carries him forward. Without deciding what he feels or naming the moment in the family’s story, we can notice how much of this image belongs to the house around him.

replacements.before: Rebati’s listening gives this literary household its quiet centre. It offers a parallel to explore alongside [AIR Cuttack](../air-cuttack.md): a voice gathering listeners beside a family member, around a radio, inside a cinema. Each setting changes who can hear and how a story reaches them.
replacements.after:
A few paragraphs later, Basudev gives Rebati a primer. Beside her father, she turns its pages, delighted by pictures of elephants, horses and cattle. She takes the book to show her mother and grandmother. The narrator measures that pleasure against grander possessions: kings have elephants and horses; others enjoy riding them; Rebi is happy with their pictures. Her grandmother responds impatiently. Before the alphabet lessons begin, the book has already set the child in motion, looking and showing. Reading this passage, we meet her pleasure before the work of learning to read.[^lit-rebati]

[AIR Cuttack](../air-cuttack.md) follows a different setting in which words reached listeners. Here, the encounter belongs to a child in a written story.
